html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. MCP: Model Context Protocol

  • What connectors are and what Google Drive, Gmail and Calendar connectors can do
  • The difference between web connectors, desktop extensions and custom connectors
  • How permissions and approvals protect you
  • What Skills are and when to use them
  • How to maintain and update Projects, knowledge and instructions over time

2Connectors

Running case

Cedarbrook's Weekly Digest

  • A project manager wants Claude to read the latest planning documents in Google Drive, check the calendar for next week's deadlines and draft an email digest
  • Pasting each document is slow and the files change daily; a connector brings the live content into the chat

A connector lets Claude access your apps and services, retrieve data and, with approval, take actions. Claude works within your own permissions: it can only reach content you could open yourself.

Type What it is Where it runs
Web (remote) connectors Cloud services you sign into: Google Workspace, Slack, Notion, GitHub, company apps In the cloud; works on web, desktop and mobile; the default choice
Desktop extensions Tools that run on your computer Claude Desktop only; for local files, local databases, OS-level access
Custom connectors Any service that supports MCP, added by URL Needs a public address; only connect servers you trust; Free plans may have only one

Google Workspace connectors

Connector Claude can Needs approval by default
Gmail Search and read email, draft, manage labels; attachments: metadata only Send, reply, forward
Google Calendar View events, find free time, create and update events, respond to invitations Changes to events (per your settings)
Google Drive Search and read Docs, Sheets, Slides, PDFs; add Docs to chats and (private) Projects; save generated files Share, move, trash
  • Each action requires your explicit approval by default; users can disable individual tools; admins on Team and Enterprise decide what can run without approval.
  • Responses cite the emails, events or documents used.
  • Added Google Docs sync: if the document changes, the chat or Project sees the update.
  • Data handling: retrieved data is tied to its chat and is deleted with the chat; Anthropic does not train its models on Gmail, Drive or Calendar connector data; data is encrypted.
  • Team and Enterprise: an owner must enable a connector for the organization, but each user still signs in individually; owners can set tool actions to Always allow, Needs approval or Blocked.
Exam tip

A connector gives Claude your access, not extra access. If you cannot open a file, neither can Claude; and actions that send or change things ask for approval first.

3Managing Connectors and Knowledge Well

Task How
Add Customize > Connectors, or the "+" menu in a chat; review the access requested; sign in
Turn on per chat Use the toggles in the Connectors menu; only enable what the task needs
Tool access mode Auto (default: Claude loads what it needs), Always available (all connectors loaded; for fewer than 10 you use constantly), On demand (loaded when needed; for 10 or more)
Reduce clutter Each connector uses conversation space and usage; turn off what you do not need
Remove Disconnect services you no longer use
Fix a broken link Disconnect and reconnect from Customize > Connectors
Check approvals Read the approval request before accepting an action that sends, shares or deletes

Uploaded knowledge versus a connector

Uploaded file Connector (live source)
Freshness A snapshot at upload time Current content (synced Docs)
Control You decide exactly what Claude sees Claude can search what you can access
Best for Stable documents (policies, guides) Frequently changing documents, email and calendar
Risk Goes stale Broad access: keep scope narrow
  • Do not connect sources you do not need. Broader access means more places for sensitive data to enter a chat (Module 13).
  • Research can use enabled connectors without asking each time; on mobile it may skip them. Check which are on.
  • Shared chats that use connector content may be restricted by the organization's settings.

4Skills

Skills are folders of instructions, scripts and resources that Claude loads dynamically for specialized tasks. They teach Claude a repeatable method, such as "build our weekly report in the company format".

Point Detail
Progressive loading Claude sees the short description first and loads the full instructions and files only when relevant, which prevents context overload
Types Anthropic skills (built-in: Excel, Word, PowerPoint, PDF), custom skills (your own), organization skills (provisioned by Team/Enterprise owners), partner skills
Requirement Code execution / Create and edit files must be on
Creating A folder with a skill file that starts with a name and a description (what it does and when to use it); optional extra files; zip it (folder name matches skill name) and upload in Customize > Skills
Good skills One specific repeatable task, clear instructions, examples, a precise description
Sharing Custom skills stay private until shared; Team and Enterprise can share or publish with review
Security Install skills only from trusted sources; review bundled scripts; never put passwords or keys in a skill

Skills vs Projects vs connectors

Gives Claude Loaded
Project Static background knowledge and instructions Always, inside the Project
Skill A procedure for a task Only when relevant, anywhere
Connector Access to data and tools When enabled for the chat
Exam tip

Background facts live in a Project; a repeatable method lives in a Skill; live data and actions come through a connector.

5Keeping Configurations Current

Configurations decay: policies change, products launch, people leave. Maintain them like any shared document.

Practice What to do
Name an owner One person is responsible for each Project, skill and shared prompt
Review on a schedule For example monthly or whenever a policy changes
Replace, don't pile up Remove old files; keep one current version; use dates or versions in filenames
Test after changes Re-run 5 to 10 sample questions, including tricky ones, and compare
Inform the team Tell users what changed and why; share new best practices
Version and log Keep a short change log of instructions and knowledge
Watch the signals Complaints, wrong answers and drift tell you what to fix (Module 15)
Mind access Remove people who left; check sharing levels; review connector scopes
Know where facts live One source of truth, referenced by the Project, not copied in many places
  • When a policy changes, update the knowledge and the instructions that mention it, then test.
  • Features and names change; check the Release notes and Help Center for new capabilities and changes [Verify live].
  • If an answer cites an outdated rule, first suspect stale knowledge, then conflicting files, then unclear instructions.
Exam tip

A connector gives Claude your access, so keep the scope narrow, read approval requests, and disconnect what you no longer use.

6Exam Q&A

S1A project manager wants Claude to work with the latest versions of Google Docs that change daily. Which approach fits best?

  • AUse the Google Drive connector (or add the Google Docs so they stay in sync)
  • BUpload a copy of each document once and never update it afterward, since uploads sync by themselves
  • CPaste the documents into every chat
  • DAsk Claude to remember them
Show the answer

Answer: A. A connector reaches current content; static uploads go stale.

S2What can Claude access through the Gmail connector?

  • AOnly email you have permission to access, and sending requires your approval by default
  • BEmail content only if you forward it manually, and only the messages that you have already read
  • CAny mailbox in the company
  • DEveryone's drafts
Show the answer

Answer: A. Connectors operate within your own permissions, with approval for actions such as sending.

S3A team has twelve connectors enabled and chats hit length limits. What is the best adjustment?

  • ATurn off connectors that are not needed and consider on-demand tool access
  • BEnable more connectors
  • CDelete the Projects
  • DAsk Claude to ignore them
Show the answer

Answer: A. Each connector uses conversation space; keep only what the task needs.

S4Which item belongs in a Skill rather than a Project?

  • AThe brand logo
  • BA repeatable procedure for building the weekly report in the standard format
  • CA list of staff birthdays
  • DThe company's return policy document
Show the answer

Answer: B. A skill packages a procedure that loads only when relevant.

S5A shared Skill comes from an unknown website. What should you do before enabling it?

  • AEnable it immediately
  • BReview its files and scripts and use it only if the source is trusted
  • CAdd your passwords to it
  • DShare it with the team first
Show the answer

Answer: B. Skills can include scripts; install only from trusted sources and review them.

S6Which TWO are good practices for keeping a Project current? Select TWO.

  • ATest with sample questions after each update
  • BKeep all old versions in knowledge for reference
  • CHide changes from the team
  • DReplace outdated files with the current version
  • ENever change the instructions
Show the answer

Answer: A, D. Replacing stale material and testing with sample questions after each change keep a Project accurate as policies and products change.

S7After the return window changed from 30 to 14 days, the assistant still says 30. What is the most likely cause?

  • AMemory is full and has to be reset before Claude can use the new return window
  • BThe model is too large and has to be replaced by a smaller one before it can learn
  • COutdated knowledge or a conflicting file or instruction still mentions 30 days
  • DClaude is broken
Show the answer

Answer: C. When an answer cites an outdated rule, first check the knowledge files and instructions for the old value before suspecting the model.

S8An owner enabled the Google Drive connector for the organization. A new employee opens Claude. What is true?

  • AThe employee has automatic access to everything that the organization stores in its Drive accounts
  • BThe employee must still sign in individually and sees only what their own account can access
  • CThe connector works without sign-in
  • DThe employee can see other users' files
Show the answer

Answer: B. Owners enable connectors, but each user authenticates and keeps their own permissions.

S9Which source is a desktop extension best suited to?

  • AA cloud service with a public sign-in
  • BA mobile-only app
  • CA website
  • DA tool that runs on your own computer, such as local files
Show the answer

Answer: D. Desktop extensions run on your computer through Claude Desktop, which suits local files and tools that have no cloud version.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Connectors Claude uses your permissions; approvals for sending, sharing, changing
Types Web (default) · desktop extensions (local) · custom (MCP, trusted only)
Google Gmail (attachment metadata only) · Calendar · Drive (docs sync)
Data Tied to the chat; deleted with it; no training on connector data
Admins Owner enables; each user signs in; Always allow / Needs approval / Blocked
Tool access Auto · Always available (fewer than 10) · On demand (10 or more)
Skills Folders of instructions; load when relevant; need code execution; trusted sources only
Compare Project = background · Skill = procedure · Connector = live data and actions
Maintain Owner · schedule · replace stale files · test · tell the team · version
